speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you've had a chronic cough and recurrent bronchitis; to help me understand your specific condition, how long has the cough been present, and do you smoke or have any other respiratory issues like wheezing or shortness of breath?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old woman. The patient has been experiencing an aggressive cough producing copious amounts of thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum for about 11 years, with exacerbations similar to the current presentation today. Reports that the cough is worse in the morning and has had multiple evaluations in the past due to recurrent bouts of bronchitis requiring antibiotics treatment. The patient is a non-smoker.

speaker: Doctor
text: That 11-year duration with thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum in a non-smoker is highly suggestive of bronchiectasis rather than simple chronic bronchitis. Given the recurrent exacerbations requiring antibiotics, have you ever undergone a CT scan or sputum culture, and do you notice any specific triggers like cold air or post-nasal drip?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Aggressive cough with thick, yellow-green sputum. I also have Cough worse in the morning, History of recurrent bronchitis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Bronchiectasis. The clinical picture of an 11-year history of chronic cough, copious purulent sputum, and recurrent exacerbations in a non-smoker is classic for this condition. To confirm the diagnosis and assess the extent of airway damage, I need to see a high-resolution CT scan of your chest. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_CT_HighResolution.
